deliverable: Every software decoder uses allocation-controlled FFmpeg plane pools. Callers explicitly supply max_software_frame_bytes in DecodeLimits and can tighten it without increasing the ceiling. Actual requested plane payload, including alignment/tail padding and idle cached buffers, is reserved before allocation. Pool reuse shares the original charge; free callbacks release it only when storage is actually destroyed. Retained frames remain valid and charged after decoder replacement/drop.
ownership: Golden decode/software_pool owns the public get_buffer2/AVBufferPool/AVBufferRef boundary and read-only lifetime observer. The allocator has a stable boxed address until all codec contexts are destroyed; slice-worker access and pool replacement are serialized. Old-layout idle buffers are released before replacements compete with still-held old frames. No private FFmpeg ABI, new worker/disposer thread, polling, image queue, readback, authored setting or UI protocol is added. Codec-private allocations remain separate.

After initial dimensions are admitted, the software decoded-plane pool is tightened to24bytes/pixel+8MiB, leaving16bytes/pixel+8MiB of that reservation for conversion/images/observers. Capacity failure maps to the existing typed Capacity/recovery path. Native/HAP have no software-plane pool. First-install CPU diagnostics project the public typed snapshot; no periodic logger.
